original_question: Consider the rational difference equations x_{n+k} = (A0 + A1 x_n + ... + Ak x_{n+k-1})/(B0 + B1 x_n + ... + Bk x_{n+k-1}) with positive-coefficient assumptions as stated in the paper. Are there periodic equations of this form that are not equivalent to the five known examples x_{n+1}=x_n, x_{n+1}=1/x_n, x_{n+2}=x_{n+1}/x_n, x_{n+2}=(1+x_{n+1})/x_n, and x_{n+3}=(1+x_{n+1}+x_{n+2})/x_n?
target_in_paper: Section 2.8, Problem 11 ('Are there rational difference equations of the form (12) that are not equivalent to the five ones given in (13)?'). ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact family (12), the core classification question about periodic recurrences of that family, and the focus on non-equivalence to the five canonical examples in (13); that is exactly the content of Problem 11. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: The coefficient assumptions should be stated explicitly: A_i,B_i ≥ 0 for 0 ≤ i ≤ k, Σ_{i=0}^k A_i > 0, Σ_{i=0}^k B_i > 0, and A_1^2 + B_1^2 ≠ 0. So the paper assumes nonnegative coefficients with positive total numerator and denominator coefficients, not that every coefficient is strictly positive. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The ambient domain is the positive real cone: each initial condition is (x_1,...,x_k) ∈ (0,∞)^k, and the recurrence is required to generate a sequence of positive real numbers. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The quantifier in 'periodic' is global over all positive initial conditions: the equation is p-periodic if x_n = x_{n+p} for every n ≥ 1 and for every initial condition in (0,∞)^k, with p the least positive integer having that property. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, the paper-specific meaning of 'equivalent' must be unpacked: besides the five basic equations, the paper also allows the step-ℓ construction sending a p-periodic k-th order recurrence to a pℓ-periodic kℓ-th order one, and the scalar unfolding y_n = a x_n with a ≠ 0; Problem 11 asks whether every periodic equation of form (12) arises from the five basic models by these constructions. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The five basic examples are not just listed formally; the paper records their periods as 1, 2, 6, 5, and 8 respectively, which helps pin down exactly which models are intended. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

A paper-faithful formulation should not import unrelated hypotheses: this problem has no homogeneity assumption, no separate polynomial degree restriction beyond the order k of the recurrence, no nilpotency condition, and no clause of the form 'for all sufficiently large m'. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

Nearby context, though not part of the open question itself, is that the paper notes a partial classification: for k ∈ {1,2,3,4,5,7,9,11} the answer is already known to be 'no', by reference [41]. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
refined_question: Do there exist integers k,p ≥ 1 and coefficients A_i,B_i ∈ [0,∞) for 0 ≤ i ≤ k, with Σ_{i=0}^k A_i > 0, Σ_{i=0}^k B_i > 0, and A_1^2 + B_1^2 ≠ 0, such that for every initial condition (x_1,...,x_k) ∈ (0,∞)^k the recurrence x_{n+k} = (A_0 + A_1 x_n + A_2 x_{n+1} + ... + A_k x_{n+k-1}) / (B_0 + B_1 x_n + B_2 x_{n+1} + ... + B_k x_{n+k-1}) defines a positive real sequence that is p-periodic in the sense that x_{n+p} = x_n for all n ≥ 1 and p is minimal, but the equation is not equivalent, in the sense defined immediately before Problem 11, to any of the five basic periodic recurrences x_{n+1}=x_n (p=1), x_{n+1}=1/x_n (p=2), x_{n+2}=x_{n+1}/x_n (p=6), x_{n+2}=(1+x_{n+1})/x_n (p=5), and x_{n+3}=(1+x_{n+1}+x_{n+2})/x_n (p=8), where equivalence means obtainable from these by the step-ℓ order/period multiplication construction and/or by the scalar unfolding y_n = a x_n with a ≠ 0? ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem in Section 2.8 rather than a broader neighboring problem. The introduction flags this topic as the 'characterization of some rational periodic difference equations,' and Section 2.8 then supplies the full setup: the family (12), the nonnegativity and positivity assumptions on coefficients, the definition of p-periodicity over all positive initial data, the five canonical examples in (13), and the paper's notion of equivalence. Only after those definitions does the paper state Problem 11 in essentially the same form as your draft. The sentence immediately after Problem 11 adds the known cases k ∈ {1,2,3,4,5,7,9,11}, citing [41]; the bibliography identifies [41] as 'On periodic rational difference equations of order k' and [35] as the broader survey 'Different approaches to the global periodicity problem.' ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
